title: ROMAN truncates toward zero, returns empty text for 0, and maps form TRUE/blank to 0 and FALSE to 4
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527, ROMAN(number, [form]) truncates number toward zero into 0..=3999 (returning empty text "" for 0 and #VALUE! outside 0..=3999) and simplifies subtractive pairs according to form in 0..=4 (returning #VALUE! outside 0..=4). An omitted, blank, or TRUE form selects classic form 0 (ROMAN(499) = "CDXCIX"), while FALSE selects the most concise form 4 (ROMAN(499, FALSE) = "ID"). Matches 2,041/2,041 full-bank rows.
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in prefix_metadata (row 197) and 2,041/2,041 full-bank ROMAN witness rows.
